candidates.exact_span: A written submission shall be provided within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what circumstances trigger awareness and the 5-day written-report obligation affects whether noncompliance reporting was required (B) and whether absence of a written report reflects a documented no-report waiver, satisfied oral reporting, or missing evidence of a required report (C).

candidates.exact_span: The period of noncompliance including exact dates and times, and if the noncompliance has not been corrected, the anticipated time it is expected to continue
candidates.computation_change_reason: How this reporting-content requirement is read determines whether available records establish bounded noncompliance periods versus leaving the temporal scope of a limit exceedance or no-data interval unresolved for missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Steps-being taken to reduce, eliminate, and prevent recurrence of the noncomplying discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what qualifies as a 'noncomplying discharge' for reporting purposes affects whether documented corrective-action reports establish a noncompliance state versus other no-data or conditional-monitoring categories when numeric results are absent.

candidates.exact_span: Any unanticipated bypass which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of 'unanticipated bypass,' 'exceeds,' and which permit provisions count as 'effluent limitation' change which numeric limits are implicated in an exceedance (A), whether 24-hour reporting was required for a bypass event (B), and whether missing bypass reports represent required-but-undocumented monitoring versus excused conditional periods (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any upset which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'upset' and whether an upset 'exceeds' an effluent limitation affects applicable limit comparisons and exceedance findings (A), applicability of the 24-hour upset-reporting obligation (B), and classification of periods without upset reports as documented non-events versus missing required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: Violation of a maximum daily discharge limitation for any of the pollutants listed by the Director in Part II (industrial permits only) of the permit to be reported within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this permit is treated as an industrial permit, which Part II pollutants carry maximum daily discharge limitations, and what constitutes a 'violation' directly changes which enforceable MDLs apply and whether measured values exceed them (A), whether 24-hour MDL-violation reporting was required (B), and whether absent MDL-violation reports indicate missing evidence of required reporting or a non-applicable requirement (C).

candidates.exact_span: The Director may waive the written report on a case-by-case basis if the oral report has been received within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a waiver was granted or oral reporting alone satisfied the obligation affects whether written reporting remained required (B) and whether lack of a written report is an established alternate compliance path versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall institute a program within 12 months of the effective date of the permit (or continue an existing one) directed towards optimizing the efficiency and extending the useful life of the facility.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of the effective date, the 12-month deadline, and whether continuing an existing program satisfies the requirement affects whether the pollution-prevention program obligation was applicable and due during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Bypasses and overflows of the tributary sewerage system and treatment works
candidates.computation_change_reason: How this pollution-prevention consideration relates to bypass/overflow events and separate 24-hour bypass-reporting duties affects whether bypass/overflow monitoring or documentation was required beyond numeric effluent sampling (B) and how undocumented bypass/overflow periods are classified when ordinary numeric results are missing (C).
